title: Cabin air: low oxygen (Earth reference, no space data)

steps.text: Look for signs of low oxygen (bluish lips, nails or skin) and measure oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
source.section: Concise guidelines for clinical practice, ABCDE (Table 3), B-Breathing

steps.text: If you are trained, give oxygen by face mask to a crewmember who has difficulty breathing and looks blue, and adjust the flow to keep oxygen saturation at 94–98 %.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
source.section: Concise guidelines for clinical practice, Use of a pulse oximetry and use of oxygen

steps.text: If oxygen saturation is below 88 %, give oxygen at a higher flow.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
